title: Add Prometheus metrics for burst saturation, denials, queue depth, and telemetry lag
author: Logan Wright
description:
Motivation: We need first-class signals to (a) protect non-burst tenants via fast detection of neighbor impact precursors and (b) make burst behavior explainable/supportable (clear denial reasons, pool saturation, and telemetry health). This PR adds a minimal, low-cardinality Prometheus metric set for burst pools and admission decisions, wired into the burst admission controller + routing call site, with guardrails to avoid tenant-level cardinality.

What’s included: (1) Pool-level saturation and supply signals: redwood_burst_pool_capacity_gpus{region,hw_class,pool} (gauge) and redwood_burst_pool_inuse_gpus{region,hw_class,pool} (gauge) and derived redwood_burst_pool_saturation_ratio{region,hw_class,pool} (gauge). (2) Admission decision counters: redwood_burst_admission_requests_total{region,hw_class,pool,decision} (counter) and redwood_burst_admission_denials_total{region,hw_class,pool,reason} (counter). (3) Queue/backpressure: redwood_burst_admission_queue_depth{region,hw_class,pool} (gauge) and redwood_burst_admission_queue_wait_seconds_bucket{region,hw_class,pool} (histogram). (4) Telemetry health/lag: redwood_burst_telemetry_lag_seconds{region,hw_class,source} (gauge) and redwood_burst_telemetry_last_update_timestamp_seconds{region,hw_class,source} (gauge). (5) Routing integration: propagate decision + denial reason into gateway stats without adding tenant_id labels; we only emit route_class and customer_tier where present (bounded sets).

Cardinality policy: This PR explicitly does NOT label metrics by tenant_id, org_id, request_id, model, or endpoint path. Allowed labels are region, hw_class, pool, decision, reason, source, plus customer_tier (gold/silver/standard) and route_class (chat/embeddings/rerank) where bounded. A lint test is included to block accidental high-cardinality label additions.

Notes on semantics: decision is one of {baseline,burst_admitted,burst_denied,fail_open,fail_closed}. Denial reason aligns with pr-23795 enums: {pool_saturated,tenant_cap_reached,fleet_safety_cap,cooldown_active,telemetry_stale,priority_budget_exhausted,internal_error}. telemetry_stale is emitted when telemetry_lag_seconds exceeds the configured freshness window at evaluation time.

Rollout/usage: Dashboards/alerts are handled in observability-pack (separate PR). For now, this PR provides the signals needed for: (a) SRE alerting on sustained saturation + rising denials, (b) gating rules to disable burst when telemetry is stale, and (c) support debug workflows (denial reason breakdowns).
commits: metrics(burst): add admission request + denial counters (decision/reason)
metrics(burst): add queue depth gauge and queue wait histogram
metrics(burst): export telemetry lag gauges and freshness timestamps
routing: emit bounded admission outcome stats (no tenant labels)
tests: add metric label allowlist + cardinality regression test
docs: add metric help strings and examples for Grafana queries
conversation: Allison Grant: Metric set looks right and label bounds are good. Can we ensure we never attach model_name or route path here? Those will explode cardinality in practice.

Logan Wright (author): Yep—added pkg/metrics/label_policy.go allowlist + a unit test that fails if any burst metrics register labels outside the bounded set. Also kept route_class instead of raw path, and no model labels.

Sean Gallagher: For SRE paging we’ll want a clean separation between "denied due to guardrail" and "denied due to internal error". Can you make sure internal_error is its own reason and emitted on evaluator exceptions?

Logan Wright (author): Added reason=internal_error for exception paths and decision=fail_closed where applicable. We still count the request in requests_total with decision=fail_closed; denials_total increments with reason=internal_error.
Peter Holtz: Queue wait histogram buckets: can we align with our standard latency buckets? Also, please confirm queue depth is per-pool (not per-tenant queue).
Logan Wright (author): Updated buckets to match pkg/metrics/latency_buckets.go (5ms..30s) and confirmed queue depth is a single per-pool gauge. No per-tenant queues are exported.
Keiko Yamamoto: telemetry_lag_seconds source label—what are the values? Please keep it bounded. Also, do we have a freshness window constant to compare against in dashboards?

Logan Wright (author): source is one of {fleet_telemetry,pool_allocator}. Both bounded. Freshness window is already in config (burst.telemetry.max_staleness_seconds); dashboards can overlay that value. This PR just exposes lag + last_update.
Allison Grant: Approved. Please make sure metric HELP strings include units (seconds/gpus).
Logan Wright (author): Done—HELP strings updated in metrics registry + helptext.yaml.
Sean Gallagher: Approved (SRE). This unblocks ENG-4833 dashboard work.
release_notes: Added Prometheus metrics for burst pool saturation, admission requests/denials (with reason codes), queue depth/wait time, and telemetry lag to support dashboards, alerting, and rollout gating.
